source.title: Optimization dependent generalization bound for ReLU networks based on sensitivity in the tangent bundle
source.authors: D'aniel R'acz; M. Petreczky; Andr'as Csert'an; Bálint Daróczy

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including its appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures whether tangent sensitivity tracks the empirical generalization gap, a related property-to-gap question. It does not test the specific magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7 or another listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports tangent-sensitivity/generalization-gap correlations. This is a different measure from every listed version, so the rows are recorded under versions ["none"]. Figure captions identify correlations but do not provide numerical correlation values.
record.test_reason: The study derives a tangent-sensitivity bound and reports tangent-sensitivity/generalization-gap correlations. It does not test any listed version: input sensitivity of parameter gradients is different from V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness. Comparing correlations at different widths does not establish V2's test-error trend beyond interpolation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish an optimization-dependent PAC bound involving tangent sensitivity under stated assumptions and report empirical correlations with generalization gaps. They acknowledge that the bound is not tight.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures tangent sensitivity rather than the magnitude-aware sharpness intervention or comparison described in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relationship differs with network width: for wide networks, different output neurons correlate with the mean gap; for lower widths, the correlation is reported only for matching per-class output neurons and per-class loss.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report correlations between tangent-sensitivity norms and empirical generalization gaps on MNIST and CIFAR-10. For 3000-wide networks, different output neurons' sensitivities correlate with the mean gap; at lower widths, the reported correlation requires matching output classes and class losses. Numerical correlation strengths are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tangent-sensitivity norms track empirical generalization gaps in the tested fully connected ReLU networks, with the reported correspondence depending on width and class matching.

record.peer_reviewed: OPT2023: 15th Annual Workshop on Optimization for Machine Learning at the 37th NeurIPS 2023
record.problems: Correlation values are not stated in the text; plotted values are described as linearly scaled for presentation. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The MNIST result is presented in a figure without a prose description of the correlation's direction or magnitude.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Test-error behavior as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests'/T2 classification conflicts with its correct observation that no listed version is measured. No verdict labels apply. The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plotted values; missing correlation coefficients are an evidence limitation, not missing results on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Test-error behavior as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Effects of dropout on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations and their relation to the generalization gap; the study measures tangent sensitivity instead.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
